sections.overview: Urania leilus is a brightly marked day-flying moth in the family Uraniidae, native to tropical South America.
sections.identification: Its black wings bear iridescent green bands, the feature reflected in its English common name.
sections.habitat: Its main range is in tropical South America east of the Andes, with records from the Amazon basin and farther south.
sections.diet: Larvae of Urania moths use Omphalea plants as food; species-specific host records are not complete in the sources consulted.
sections.behavior: Urania moths undertake periodic long-distance migrations, although the timing and routes of this species are not fully described here.
sections.reproduction: Research on Urania treats reproductive behavior together with the moths’ Omphalea host plants, but the summaries consulted do not detail this species’ egg-laying.
sections.ecology: Smithsonian researchers link Urania migration to changing host-plant suitability: repeated larval feeding can increase defensive alkaloids in Omphalea.
sections.conservation: The sources consulted focus on distribution and host-plant ecology and do not provide a conservation category for U. leilus.
